title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a blackboard-style summary, probably for the 1976 IHES lecture, of the bar construction and how it is used to compute the homology of Eilenberg–MacLane spaces. That computation is the input for the previous page's discussion of the Steenrod algebra, the Milnor dual and derived symmetric powers L Sym^{p^s} K(F_p,n).

(1) Setting: A is a differential graded F_p-algebra with an augmentation ε: A → F_p.

(2) Two bar constructions are introduced.
- B(A) is the acyclic, two-sided bar construction. It is drawn as the simplicial object ... A⊗A⊗A ⇉ A⊗A → A, with faces given by the multiplication μ and by 1⊗ε. It is the algebraic analogue of EG, i.e. of Z[EG].
- B̄(A) is the reduced bar construction. It is the simplicial object ... A⊗A ⇉ A ⇉ F_p, circled on the page, whose faces use μ and ε. It is the analogue of BG, i.e. of Z[BG].

(3) The model case: for A = Z[G], the simplicial abelian group ... ZG^3 ⇉ ZG^2 ⇉ ZG, using ZG^2 = ZG⊗ZG, is the chain complex of EG. So it is 'the bar construction on the algebra ZG' (Bar consts sur l'alg ZG). Passing to coinvariants gives the chains of BG.

(4) Iteration: for A = Z[K(G,n)], the group ring of the simplicial abelian group K(G,n), one has B̄(A) ≃ Z[BK(G,n)] = Z[K(G,n+1)]. Iterating B̄ therefore computes H_*(K(G,n)). This is the Eilenberg–MacLane method.

(5) Product structure: if A is commutative, then μ: A⊗A → A is an algebra homomorphism. Using the Eilenberg–Zilber (shuffle) map B̄(A)⊗B̄(A) ⇄ B̄(A⊗A) and then B̄(μ): B̄(A⊗A) → B̄(A), one obtains the shuffle product making B̄(A) a commutative algebra.

(6) The marginal note 'a⊗⋯⊗a, n fois' with 'd' and 'A commutative' points to elements [a|a|…|a] in the bar construction. For a commutative A these give divided powers, since the shuffle power [a]^n = n![a|…|a]. This is Cartan's divided-power structure on the bar construction, which links to the lecture's theme of divided-power de Rham complexes. The page itself contains no proof, only a sketch.
errors: No mathematical errors. Notational looseness only: the same symbol ⇉ is used for whole simplicial objects whose face maps are left unspecified.
B̄(Z[K(G,n)]) ≃ Z[K(G,n+1)] holds up to quasi-isomorphism (normalized chains), as the '~' indicates.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a textbook summary of the classical Eilenberg–MacLane and Cartan machinery (bar construction, shuffle product, homology of K(G,n)), recalled as background for the lecture. Nothing on the page goes beyond the 1950s literature.
transcription_corrections: 'E Zilber' should read Eilenberg–Zilber (the Eilenberg–Zilber shuffle map).
In the second simplicial row, the 'd' written under A is the differential of the dga, attached to the marginal note 'a⊗⋯⊗a (n fois)'.
'A —Z[?]' near 'A⊗A' is probably 'A → ε' (the augmentation) or a scratched-out symbol, not Z.
'I⊗A⊗A → A hom d'alg' most likely reads 'A⊗A → A hom d'alg' (μ is an algebra map when A is commutative); the 'I' is a stray mark or bullet.
Page number in the image is 369 (archive numbering), not 367.
